wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are trying to orient themselves on the country, its geography and its history. It rises when Iran becomes the subject of an unfolding event rather than a background one.
wiki-iran.recent: Hostilities resumed after a month's pause: US strikes killed 11 people, including five at a wedding in Sirik, and Iran struck two US airbases in Jordan while a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Vance declined to call it a war, and the Pentagon extended Gulf deployments into 2027.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is sold against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: The Strait of Hormuz closure holds as US and Iranian forces trade attacks, with two tankers attacked leaving Hormuz and a supertanker stopped after hitting mines there. Washington has adopted a tanker-for-tanker policy, striking two Iranian tankers. Brent reached 105.3 on Jul 23 and sits at 96.02, high enough that Fed hike odds jumped to two-in-three.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of American light sweet crude, the benchmark US oil is priced against and the reference for North American refiners. It moves on supply — an outage, a sanction, a strait — and petrol, freight and airfares follow it.
wti.recent: US drones struck two Iranian oil tankers under a tanker-for-a-tanker policy, and prices jumped on the supply risk: Brent rose 3% to $90.97 as the strikes widened the target set from military to economic infrastructure. Washington's Venezuela oil deal and India's defence of Russian crude purchases have kept barrels flowing elsewhere.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and used to price most American gas contracts. It sets the cost of heating, electricity from gas-fired plants, fertilizer and the LNG the US ships abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: US gas eased to $2.90 while Europe went the other way: European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour on 2 September, a three-year high, with EU storage near 64% and buyers competing for LNG spot cargoes. That pull reached importers rather than Henry Hub — Delhi raised CNG by ₹3.89 a kg and Pakistan apologized for night blackouts after a delayed RLNG cargo.

wheat.standing: The benchmark price of a tonne of milling wheat on world markets, the grain that feeds more people than any other. Harvest weather, export bans and freight costs move it, and bread prices and food-aid budgets follow.
wheat.recent: The rise tracks a developing El Niño the UN calls near certain to persist to February and possibly the strongest in decades, a pattern that thins monsoon margins in South Asia and dries the Horn of Africa. Funding is tightening alongside it: WFP halved its West Bank caseload on cost, not access.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the planet and the thinnest of the major grain markets, where a single exporter's ban can reset the price for importing countries across Asia and West Africa.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen about 16% over the series, sitting at $464 a tonne against a low of $330.6 in Oct 2025 and a high of $555.1 in Sep 2024. The coverage does not explain the move.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in almost everything that uses it. Demand comes from grids, buildings, cables and motors, which makes it the closest thing markets have to a gauge of electrification.
copper.recent: Copper sits near its series high after a long climb, and the demand story is visible in the grid: AI load is reinventing the transformer, electric vehicles are straining voltage on distribution networks, and Washington has banned foreign grid parts on security grounds. Germany is now investigating sabotage at two substations.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, and the reference price for mortgages, corporate debt and sovereign borrowing worldwide. It is the benchmark almost every other long-dated asset is priced against.
us-10y.recent: The yield rose to 4.79% on Sep 1 from 4.38% in late June as an oil shock reversed the usual wartime reflex: with Brent near $95–97 on the resumed Iran strikes, the market moved from expecting a Fed cut to pricing a possible hike, and bonds were sold rather than bought. Thirty-year yields reached 5.3%, a 2007 level.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US-listed companies, and the standard proxy for the American stock market. Pensions, index funds and corporate valuations worldwide are benchmarked against it.
sp500.recent: The index sits below its Aug 13 high of 7799 as bond yields hit multi-decade highs on inflation fears and the dollar fell to its weakest since May on Waller comments. The AI trade still carries the market: Nvidia pledged $500 billion to its own buyers, a vendor-financing loop that keeps demand on its own balance sheet.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by chipmakers and software firms, which makes it the closest thing to a live price on the technology trade.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after Nvidia's $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face and its $3.5 billion convertible stake in MediaTek, two deals that put one chipmaker on both the compute and distribution sides of open-weight AI. Antitrust news cut the other way: a judge ruled Google need not sell its ad exchange, while the FTC sued Amazon over $20 billion in advertiser overcharges.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price of a gallon of regular petrol across US filling stations, surveyed weekly. It follows crude and refining margins with a lag, and it is the number most Americans feel a fuel market through.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining, not crude, is where the strain sits. Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries pushed Moscow to import fuel and lower its standards, with Putin conceding "not all fuel issues have been resolved," and forecourt prices climbed elsewhere too — South Africa's petrol rose R1.34 a litre and Pakistan raised petrol by Rs1.08.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas delivered into the Dutch TTF hub, Europe's benchmark for wholesale gas. It sets what utilities pay to heat homes and run industry, and because Europe now buys much of its gas as seaborne LNG, it competes directly with Asian buyers.
natgas-ttf.recent: European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour on Wednesday, a three-year high, as EU storage sat near 64% ahead of winter and US-Iran hostilities pushed LNG buyers into competition for the same spot cargoes. Europe buys almost no Iranian gas — the move is displacement, not lost supply. Delhi's CNG price rose ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg on the same LNG squeeze.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option premiums. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear in equity markets.
vix.recent: Volatility has drained out of the market over the past three months, with the index down roughly a fifth from its 10 June high of 22.22 and sitting near the 14.25 floor set on 14 August. The input does not identify what drove the decline.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's exchange rate against the dollar, and the price at which Pakistan pays for everything it imports — crude, palm oil, machinery, fertiliser. It also sets the local-currency cost of servicing the country's foreign debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee held in a narrow band, touching 278.8 on Aug 31 before easing to 277.6. Two of the props under it are external: EU figures show Pakistan received €732 million in 2024 tariff exemptions under GSP+, a preference tied to reforms the Commission's review found only partly delivered, and diesel — which peaked at Rs520 a litre in April — is taxed at Rs114 rather than subsidised.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted against the dollar. It is the price at which Africa's largest oil exporter converts crude earnings into imported fuel, food and machinery, so it sets the cost of almost everything sold in the country.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed against the dollar over the month, from 1,365 on Aug 8 to 1,323. Foreign reserves hit a 20-year high in late August, with Moody's rewarding Nigeria's austerity, and FTSE Russell will reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified on September 21. Petrol imports, which drain dollars, ran at 43% of supply in July.

fx-egp.standing: The price of Egypt's currency against the dollar, set on a market since the 2024 float. It sets the cost of the wheat, fuel and fertiliser Egypt imports, and the burden of the dollar debt the state has to service.
fx-egp.recent: The pound weakened past 51 to the dollar on Sep 3, days after the US cut a major Egyptian bank off from the global financial system on Aug 28. The slide ran through Xi Jinping's first state visit to Cairo in a decade, where Egypt sought leverage from a position of weakness.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira's exchange rate against the US dollar. Turkey imports most of its energy and much of its food in dollars, so the rate sets domestic prices, and it is the number Turkish households watch to judge inflation.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low against the dollar through a month of Turkish security news rather than economic policy: Erdogan defended Turkey's SCO push as a "360-degree" foreign policy and not an abandonment of the West, Ankara summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships, and the Mecca defence pact's first committee met in Istanbul.

fx-bdt.standing: The exchange rate of Bangladesh's currency against the US dollar. The taka sets the import bill for a country that buys its fuel, food and cotton in dollars, and it is the number the garment industry's export earnings convert back into.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka steadied through late August, easing from 124 on Aug 7 to 122 on Aug 19 and settling near 122.6. Dhaka confirmed a purchase of Chinese J-10CE fighter jets on Aug 29, and Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected president on Aug 21 — but nothing in the window explains the currency's move.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's currency against the US dollar, the price at which Southeast Asia's largest economy trades. It carries the cost of imported fuel and food, and the burden of dollar-denominated debt held by Indonesian companies and the state.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah has firmed from 17,920 on Aug 6 to 17,640, reaching its strongest level of the period as Jakarta pushed its trade alignment eastward. Prabowo Subianto confirmed parliament had ratified the free trade agreement with the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union and asked for early entry into force, opening tariff-free access for palm oil, textile and coffee exporters.

fx-lbp.standing: The exchange rate between Lebanon's currency and the US dollar. After the banking collapse wiped out most of its value, the pound is the price at which salaries, savings and imported food, fuel and medicine are all reckoned in a heavily dollarised economy.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has been close to flat for a month, drifting between 89,280 on Aug 8 and 89,980 on Aug 31 while the war in the south continued: Lebanon's health ministry put the death toll from Israeli attacks at 4,350, and Israeli troops held Christian border villages including Ain Ebel.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate between China's currency and the US dollar, managed within a band the central bank sets each morning rather than floated freely. It prices the world's largest exporter's goods, and moves in it ripple through every supply chain that starts in China.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan strengthened steadily through the month, touching its firmest level of the series on Sep 4 after weakening to 6.749 on Aug 6. China's factory gauge rose to 51.5 in August, and Beijing pushed on several fronts at once: Xi Jinping toured Cairo, and Shanghai's crude benchmark gained pricing independence.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar. India imports most of its crude oil and pays for it in dollars, so a weaker rupee raises the cost of fuel and everything moved by it, and sets the return on money invested in Indian assets.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee firmed through the window, reaching 94.38 on Sep 3 from its Aug 20 high of 95.77. India's economy grew 7.8% in the June quarter, though the prior-year base was cut 7%, from Rs 86.05 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore, which raises the ratio without extra output. New Delhi held to discounted Russian crude, its largest supplier.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate of Brazil's currency against the US dollar, priced as reais per dollar. Brazil sells soy, iron ore, oil and coffee in dollars, so the rate sets what the world's commodity buyers pay and what Brazilian borrowers owe.
fx-brl.recent: The real held a narrow range and finished slightly stronger, at 5.102 to the dollar after a high of 5.222 on Aug 15. Two domestic pressures ran through the month: the collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe, and a new poll on Sep 2 showing Brazil's president losing his lead. Neither produced a decisive move in the currency.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate of Mexico's peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so the rate carries every shift in US trade policy, demand and interest rates.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso has firmed by about 2 percent over the past month, from 17.24 on Aug 6 to 16.90 on Sep 4, its strongest level in the series. Nothing in the material here accounts for the move.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, quoted here inverted as euros per dollar. It is the world's second reserve currency and the second most traded pair, so it sets the terms on which the eurozone's imports, exports and debt are priced.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted lower across a month dominated by European security rather than economics: Germany formally blamed Russia for the Leipzig drone plot, closed Russia's consulate in Bonn, and Moscow answered by shutting three Goethe-Institut centres. Volkswagen's announcement of 50,000 further job cuts landed in the same week.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate of Japan's currency against the dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker yen. It moves on the gap between Japanese and US interest rates, and it sets the price of everything an island that imports its energy has to buy.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen slid past 160 per dollar on 31 August as the rate gap and energy costs widened, putting traders on intervention watch. It has since recovered to 156.4, with the dollar falling to its weakest since May on Waller's comments; US Treasury Secretary Bessent had urged Japan to raise rates.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, the price at which the world buys and sells claims on the Russian economy. It moves on oil revenue, capital controls and sanctions, and import prices inside Russia follow it.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened past 87 to the dollar on Sep 3 as sanctions pressure and retaliation widened: Germany closed Russia's Bonn consulate over the Leipzig drone attack, Moscow shut three Goethe-Institut centres, and Norway seized the Professor Molchanov under a Hague arbitration award. Households moved 4.2 trillion rubles into cash.

fx-zar.standing: The exchange rate between South Africa's rand and the US dollar. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and because South Africa imports its fuel and prices its mining exports in dollars, the rate feeds straight into what households pay at the pump.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed to 16.05 over the month, off its 16.36 low on Aug 7 and near the 15.92 high of Aug 26. The gain did not reach the forecourt: petrol rose R1.34 a litre on Tuesday, as the fuel formula passed through costs the stronger currency was expected to offset.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin, the largest and oldest cryptocurrency, quoted around the clock on exchanges worldwide. It has no coupon, no issuer and no closing bell, so it prices whatever traders think a fixed supply is worth at any hour.
btc.recent: The rise from $64,000 followed a Treasury tweak in late August, and the move up to $80,020 was driven by a short squeeze rather than fresh leverage. ETF inflows ran at $800 million over two days, and BlackRock cut its in-kind swap threshold from $25 million to $1 million.

eth.standing: The native token of Ethereum, the largest programmable blockchain, paid as the fee for every transaction and contract that runs on it. Its price tracks demand for the network itself, from lending apps to stablecoin transfers.
eth.recent: Ether ran from $1,871 on 11 August to $2,515 on 22 August, a rise CoinDesk tied to a squeeze-led rally that decimated bears and left ether crushing bitcoin. The move came as the US securities regulator proposed a crypto rulebook and an attacker drained $8.5 million from Ethereum lending app Term Finance by buying voting power.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by physical gold in a vault, so its price tracks a troy ounce of bullion. It carries gold's role as the asset people buy when they doubt currencies, central banks or the value of holding anything else.
paxg.recent: Gold ran up to $4,672 on Aug 25 as bitcoin and gold priced Warsh's Jackson Hole speech and the question of Fed independence, then eased to $4,468. Physical demand shows in the parallel markets: street dealers in Kassala now outbid Sudan's licensed gold market, and Islamic State buried $47 million in gold and cash near Deir ez-Zor.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A daily count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence — a rough gauge of public curiosity about the field rather than of the technology itself, rising when the subject reaches people who do not follow it professionally.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership climbed with a dense week of AI news: Nvidia agreed to pay $12.9 billion for Hugging Face, OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra to developers, and ChatGPT, Claude and Grok went down at the same time on Thursday. The EU also brought ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox under its 'very large platform' rules.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia — a general country page whose traffic sits at a high baseline and lifts when the country is at the centre of a story, making it a rough gauge of how widely a Russia event travelled beyond people already following it.
wiki-russia.recent: Readership held near its baseline through a run of escalation with Germany: Berlin formally blamed Russia for the failed Leipzig drone attack, closed Russia's consulate in Bonn, and Moscow answered by summoning the German chargé d'affaires and shutting three Goethe-Institut centres.

wiki-pakistan.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan — a rough gauge of how much of the world is trying to read up on a nuclear-armed state of some 240 million people, and one that tends to rise when the country enters a crisis rather than a news cycle.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Readership has fallen by about a quarter from its 14 August peak, and the events that carried it were mostly late-month: the hospital nursery fire in Islamabad that killed 14 newborns on 26 August, Imran Khan's return to jail after a medical checkup, and army chief Asim Munir's Tehran visit and call with Trump on Pakistan's Iran mediation. The Mecca defence pact's first committee meeting in Istanbul followed on 31 August.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on China — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking up the country itself rather than any single story about it.
wiki-china.recent: The peak on Aug 13 sat in a run of flooding on the Nepal-China border, where deaths topped 1,000 and hundreds of tourists went missing as a trade corridor closed. Since then the reading has stayed elevated through Xi Jinping's visit to Cairo, Vietnam's demand that construction halt on two Paracel features, and Taiwan's espionage accusation at the Pacific Islands Forum.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that every tanker leaving the Gulf must pass through. It is narrow enough that a single navy, or a single minefield, can price the oil the rest of the world burns.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: US and Iranian forces resumed strikes across the Gulf: a US drone attack killed five at a wedding at Sirik, Iran hit two US airbases in Jordan, and a supertanker stopped after hitting mines in the strait. Iran now says transit requires Tehran's permission; Brent rose 3% to $90.97. Trump separately proposed renaming the strait.

wiki-india.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on India each day. It tracks where general curiosity lands rather than what happened, so it rises when the country enters a story large enough to send readers looking for the basics.
wiki-india.recent: The peak on Sep 1 tracked Bishkek, where Modi met Putin at the SCO summit and urged peace in Ukraine while India kept buying Russian crude as Moscow's second-largest oil customer. Jaishankar then defended those purchases in Kyiv, and Belgium's prime minister backed India on cross-border terrorism on Sep 3.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up rather than a measure of anything happening inside it.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 24 August peak followed the strike on an arms depot near Kyiv, where stored shells rather than the strike itself killed 37, and the war then widened beyond the front: Germany formally blamed Russia for the Leipzig airport drone attack, Turkey summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on its ships, and Norway seized the Professor Molchanov at Barentsburg.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed as the US-Iran campaign moved onto the water: two Iranian oil tankers were struck by US drones, two more were attacked leaving Hormuz, and a supertanker was stopped after hitting mines. Last week's transits ran 57% below the 90-day baseline, with Brent up 3% to $90.97 and European gas above €75 per megawatt-hour.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic runs about a fifth below its 90-day baseline after the war on the Yemeni coast reached shipping itself: a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, the same day Saudi Arabia shelled villages in Razih district on the Saada border. The low of 14 vessels came on 5 August.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic has recovered through the window, running about 4.6% above its own 90-day baseline and reaching 57 vessels a day on 11 August, well up from the 22 recorded on 16 June. The Houthis said they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia on 24 August, a reminder of the Red Sea risk that pushed carriers away in the first place.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has held roughly flat across the window, running about 8% below its 90-day baseline in the past week, with a low of 170 vessels on 19 July and a peak of 269 on 27 July. Seas were calm, with waves under half a metre, and nothing in the record explains the softer recent count.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic has run about 14% below its own 90-day baseline in the past week, with a collapse to 28 vessels on 12 July before a rebound to 401 the following day. Nothing in the week's news explains the shortfall; seas stayed calm, with a maximum wave height of 1.2 metres.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits are running about 4% below their 90-day baseline, at 31 vessels a day against a July 13 high of 83. The UN says odds are near 100% that El Niño persists to February and could be the strongest in decades — the pattern that dries the canal's watershed and forces the authority to cut daily slots.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic sits about a fifth below its 90-day baseline, and the strait's approaches have been unusually costly: 10 crew are missing after two ships collided off Istanbul on 3 September, near Silivri. Turkey also summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on its ships in the Black Sea, the trade the strait carries.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic sits near its 90-day baseline, with the low of 112 vessels a day on Jul 11 and the high of 163 on Jun 13 both inside the usual range, and calm water at a maximum wave height of 0.8 metres. The pressure on this strait is at its edges rather than on its shipping: more than 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta in July, and Morocco deported over 4,000 from Tangier in 20 days.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has run close to its own 90-day baseline, within about a percent, with the range across the window from 186 vessels on Aug 1 to 126 on Aug 3 and 147 at the latest reading. Waves peaked at a modest 2.2 metres and no weather alert was in force. Nothing in the record explains the swing beyond ordinary variation.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic has drifted back down after the July peak, running near its 90-day baseline. Attacks on tankers continued through late August — a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker at Yanbu, and US drones struck two Iranian oil tankers — but the strikes have not pushed traffic back onto the long route around Africa. Waves reached 4.1 metres.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, down from 23 vessels a day in mid-June, with no movement since 17 July. The strait sits inside a war that has moved decisively onto the water: Ukrainian sea drones hit a vessel in Sochi, further along the same Black Sea coast, and Zelenskyy has named Moscow and St. Petersburg as targets.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its range, some 2.7% below where it stood a month ago, after a high of 11150 on Jun 16. Riyadh spent the period signing a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey in Mecca, whose first committee met in Istanbul, and negotiating a nuclear deal with Washington; neither explains the drift.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index has drifted lower across the window, down 0.8% on the day and about a quarter of its June 18 peak of 14,830 gone by September 3. Ankara summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships, and a cargo ship sank off Istanbul on September 3 with ten crew missing.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index has drifted down from its Jun 18 high of 6270 as the Gulf security picture hardened. The UAE downed an Iranian drone over its territorial waters on 31 August after the US and Iran exchanged attacks, and Bessent has targeted banks in the UAE over Iran ties. Hotel demand cratered to 7% of normal levels.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted down from its Aug 26 high of 1749 through a fortnight in which prosecutors charged former prime minister Ismail Sabri with concealing $40 million in assets, and Putrajaya's plan to return 1,476 Myanmar nationals drew a public disavowal from the UN refugee agency. It sits at 1707, still above its Jul 1 low of 1657.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index reached its high of 6,668 on Sep 3, the day Prabowo Subianto said parliament had ratified Indonesia's free trade agreement with the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union and pushed for early entry into force — tariff-free access to a 180-million-person market for palm oil, textile and coffee exporters.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index sits well below its late-June high, caught between a falling yen and the prospect of tighter money. The yen fell past 160 per dollar on 31 August, putting traders on intervention watch, while US Treasury Secretary Bessent urged Japan to raise rates; Fed hike odds then jumped to two-in-three as oil rose.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits near its 65-day high after August's run to 26,010 on Aug 21, with China's factory gauge rising to 51.5 in August. The venue's pull is weaker than the level suggests: Shein listed in Hong Kong at $26.3bn, a discounted debut, while a US trade group pushed to ban Chinese cars.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits near 3,956, down about 2.5% over the window from its 4,163 high on Jun 22, with the low of 3,764 on Jul 17. The board's backdrop is external pressure: Treasury is rallying G20 partners against China's surplus, a US trade group wants Chinese cars banned, and Vietnam and Taiwan have both escalated. August's factory gauge rose to 51.5.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has fallen roughly a fifth from its June peak while the Bank of Korea kept tightening, hiking to 3.00% in a second consecutive increase that prioritised financial stability. Political noise added to it: the Unification Church leader was jailed for bribing officials, and Lee reshuffled finance and defence, raising Lee Hyoung-il to finance minister.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the upper end of its 66-day range after a run of domestic data and policy news: August vehicle sales rose, with Honda's two-wheelers up 8% at 579,000 units, while India revised its GDP base down by 7%, shrinking the denominator against which growth is measured. Sun Pharma tied its US Medicaid prices to its own floor.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index reached 5812 on Sep 4, the top of a 66-day climb of nearly 15% from its Jun 10 low of 4959. The coverage from Singapore points at the financial-technology side of that trade rather than the listed banks: crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion, and Bitget, half of whose 125 million users are Asian, opened talks with BlackRock.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Nvidia's $3.5 billion convertible stake option in MediaTek sent that stock up 10% on 1 September and carried the index with it. The rise came alongside Taiwan's six-year hunt for undeclared Chinese chip labs poaching engineers, and an indictment of nine people, an Nvidia manager among them, over AI server smuggling.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its 33-day range after a 3.5% single-day fall, having slipped from its 17 July high of 1,639 to 1,581. Nothing in the window explains the drop, though the market trades against an unresolved question over Thailand's semiconductor plan and its Washington problem.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near 6,090 after a 4.91% single-day fall, having ranged between 5,879 on Jun 8 and 6,404 on Jul 17. Nothing in the Manila news of the past week explains the drop.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index slid on 1 September after Trump's "hit them hard" vow, ending a slide from the 9,272 high of 6 August. Domestic pressure came from housing: home prices fell for a fifth straight month as homebuyer numbers collapsed, and KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index climbed to a high of 118,200 on Aug 28 before easing, leaving it up 3.3% over the window and 1.4% on the day. The coverage in this period turned on domestic fiscal and policy matters rather than the market: R88.6bn sitting unclaimed in dormant accounts and pensions, and petrol rising R1.34 a litre despite a stronger rand.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index climbed to a series high of 185,200 on Sep 2 after the collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe raised questions about Brazilian bank supervision rather than the market as a whole. A new poll showing Brazil's socialist president losing his lead landed the same day.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index has drifted lower across the window, down about 3% from its 22 July high of 3,380,000 and off 1.5% on the day. The clearest political development in the period is Trump saying the US position on the Falklands is 'one of many' under review, raising doubts over Washington's backing for Britain in the dispute with Argentina.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index climbed through a tariff fight rather than falling with it: Canada answered US duties with a 'dollar for dollar' list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, refused US relief on heavy trucks, and Ontario Premier Doug Ford backed retaliation reaching to power exports. The Aug 25 high of 36,960 came the day that matching list landed.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range, with the Aug 13 high of 7799 barely above the current 7748. Renewed US strikes on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz closure have pushed energy prices and long rates up rather than equities down, while dealmaking continued: Nvidia is paying $12.9 billion for Hugging Face.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a run that began from the June low. London itself has been the story: the exchange set out plans for tokenized UK shares, and Dangote Cement booked a London investor day ahead of a listing, choosing the deeper market over Lagos. Brent rose 3% to $90.97 on strikes on Iran, lifting the energy names.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index sits near the top of its range despite a fortnight of escalation between Berlin and Moscow: Germany formally blamed Russia for the Leipzig airport drone attack, closed Russia's consulate in Bonn, and is investigating two substations hit with homemade explosives. Volkswagen announced 50,000 more job cuts on 3 September.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index sits near the top of a two-month range, having climbed from 8150 on Jun 3 to a high of 8726 on Aug 10 before easing to 8286. Paris-listed defence and space work drew the period's contracts: Sweden signed a €4.3 billion deal on 31 August for four French frigates from Naval Group, and the European Space Agency awarded €544 million to three launcher startups.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing about 5% over the summer, with the high on Aug 13 and the low on Jun 5. European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour on Wednesday, a three-year high, with storage entering the winter at a record low.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range, close to the 20,210 high of Aug 11, having gained roughly a tenth over the period. Spain's domestic news has run to migration rather than markets: protests over the Ceuta crossings, where more than 72,000 crossed in July, and Italy's renewal of Schengen border checks with Spain to September 15.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index has climbed through the summer to 52,250, up 4.4% over the window, with the peak of 53,720 on Aug 7 and the low of 49,890 on Jun 5. Neither the renewed Schengen border suspension with Spain, extended to September 15, nor the wider bond slump has broken the run.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index has climbed roughly eight percent across the window, from its June 3 low of 13,220 to a August 10 peak of 14,630, and sits near the top of that range at 14,360. Nothing in the available material accounts for the move.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index touched its 66-day high of 3331 on Aug 28, days before Stockholm signed a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates from Naval Group at €1.1 billion each — an order placed abroad rather than with a domestic yard. It has since slipped 1.3% to 3266.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever the case for a cut or a hike strengthens.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The market swung on an oil shock: Brent near $95–97 after the resumed Iran strikes turned an expected Fed cut into a possible hike, and the no-change price fell to 41 on Sep 2. Warsh said the Fed will have "work to do" if inflation doesn't fade. It has since recovered to 59 as shares and bonds rallied.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The English Wikipedia article on the 47th US president, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises and falls with what the presidency does, which makes it a rough gauge of how far a decision has travelled beyond the news cycle.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Readership more than doubled over the week as US strikes on Iran resumed, killing five at a wedding near Sirik and eleven in all, and Brent crude rose 3% to $90.97. Trump had posted a fake video of the Kharg Island terminal exploding, and on 3 September a federal judge in Baltimore enjoined his second birthright citizenship order.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United States. Attention to a country's reference page tends to track the moments when it is doing something abroad, or something is being done to it.
wiki-united-states.recent: The rise through late August tracked the return of open fighting with Iran: US strikes resumed on 30 August after a month's pause, a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on 31 August, and by 2 September both sides were surveying damage from a night of strikes that killed 11. Venezuela ran alongside it, with Maduro posting from US detention.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The first cryptocurrency, a fixed-supply digital asset settled on a public ledger with no issuer or central bank behind it. Its price sets the tone for the rest of the crypto market and for the companies, funds and exchanges built on top of it.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Readership followed a violent price week: Bitcoin surged to $80,020, up 23.7%, in what turned out to be a short squeeze rather than a leveraged rally, and the $77,000 rally paid market makers who took no view on price. Around the peak, a shariah board cleared Bitcoin trading and Rakbank Islamic opened it inside its platform.

wiki-nepal.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan country of about 30 million between India and China. Readership climbs when the country is in the news and settles back afterwards.
wiki-nepal.recent: A glacial lake outburst on the Nepal-China border sent a flash flood down the valley on 26 August, killing at least 95 that day and leaving hundreds missing, including 400 tourists; the toll passed 1,000 and later 5,000. A second lake formed days later, and China warned of a dam-break risk.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US central bank charges banks to borrow overnight, and the anchor under almost every other price of money. Mortgages, corporate loans and dollar debt across the world reprice from it.
fed-funds.recent: The rate has been held at 3.75% since December 2025, but the market has stopped expecting the next move to be down. Brent near $95–97 on the resumed Iran strikes turned the cut trade into a hike trade, with hike odds at two-in-three, and the long end sold off with it: the 10-year Treasury yield hit 4.81% and the 30-year mortgage rate 6.71%.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays banks on money parked with it overnight, and the floor under every euro-area borrowing cost. It sets what savers earn, what mortgages cost and how the euro trades against other currencies.
ecb-rate.recent: The rate has held at 2.25% since the ECB stopped cutting, well below the 3.5% of Sep 2024 and just above the Jun 2025 low of 2%. The euro-area path has diverged from peers: the Bank of Korea hiked to 3.00% in August and markets now favor a September hike from the Fed, while global bond yields hit multi-decade highs on inflation fears.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans who want work and cannot find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when it sets interest rates, and the one voters feel first.
us-unemployment.recent: The rate stands at 4.1%, unchanged over the window and near the bottom of its recent range — down from the 4.5% high of November 2025, and just above the 4.0% low of January 2025. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and one of its two largest economies. The count rises when something there reaches a global audience, and falls back to a wide baseline drawn from students, travellers and the diaspora.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Uber shut down in Nigeria and Uganda with immediate effect on 2 September, with no notice to drivers or passengers and no wind-down for contractors. Readership had been at its lowest of the month on 28 August, and turned back up as the exit spread across outlets from the BBC to RT.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party built around Vladimir Putin, wins the most seats at the next State Duma election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The contract firmed through a month in which the war widened outward rather than at home: Germany formally blamed Russia for a drone attack on Leipzig airport, the EU summoned Russia's envoy over it, and Norway seized the research vessel Professor Molchanov at Barentsburg on a Naftogaz arbitral award. It touched 75% on Aug 30 and sits at 70%.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington lifts its naval blockade of Iran by a set date. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for it happening — a running read on how plausible an exit looks.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The odds collapsed from 24% on Aug 27 to 5% by Sep 3 as the campaign extended rather than wound down. The Pentagon pushed Gulf deployments into 2027, US strikes resumed around Hormuz — killing eleven, including five at a wedding at Sirik — and Washington adopted a tanker-for-tanker targeting policy.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States mounts a ground invasion of Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, so it tracks how much of the market's money is behind the most extreme step available to Washington.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Odds slipped from 18% on Aug 7 to 13% by Aug 28 even as the air campaign widened — US strikes resumed after a month's pause, 11 were killed including a wedding party at Sirik, and Iran hit two US airbases in Jordan. Traders read the Pentagon's extension of Gulf deployments into 2027 as a long air war, not a prelude to boots on the ground.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A prediction market on whether Israel and Iran will hold a ceasefire by a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each round of strikes, mediation and retaliation rather than with any official statement.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The price sat at 63% on Aug 10 and has climbed since, reaching 89% on Aug 25 before easing to 87% — even as US strikes on Iran resumed on Aug 30, killed 11 including a wedding party at Sirik, and a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The coverage does not explain the divergence.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves as the field, the courts and the campaign change around him.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: The contract rose from 26 on Aug 5 to 44 on Sep 4, its high for the window, a gain of about two thirds. Nothing in the material here explains the shift.

xag.standing: A token backed one-for-one by allocated physical silver, so it tracks the metal's spot price. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics, brazing — so it answers to investors and factories at once.
xag.recent: Silver ran from $50.58 on Aug 24 to $69.42 on Aug 28, better than a third in four days, and has since eased back to $65.79, leaving it up about 17% over the month. Nothing available accounts for the jump.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The Wikipedia article on petroleum — crude oil, the refined fuels made from it, and the industry that moves them. Readership rises when supply is disrupted or ownership of reserves changes hands, which makes it a rough gauge of who is trying to understand the oil story.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Attention tracked the seizure and repricing of oil supply. The Aug 13 peak came amid the Venezuela reserves story that would put 65 billion barrels under a US contract, with Machado questioning the deal's legitimacy; readership held up as Brent rose 3% to $90.97 on Iran strikes and two tankers were attacked leaving Hormuz.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether J.D. Vance becomes the Republican presidential nominee in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on party signals, rival entrances and anything that changes who controls the primary field.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.recent: The month's move came against a rough stretch for prediction markets rather than any named development in the Republican field. A White House teleprompter operator paid a fine over bets placed on the president's speeches, the Ninth Circuit ruled that sports bets are not "swaps" and confirmed state powers over the venues, and 152 Polymarket wallets were shown trading a 97.2% win rate. The contract rose from 43 on Aug 8 to a high of 53 on Sep 3.

poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Anthropic will be judged to have the leading AI model at the period's end. It prices a race between a handful of frontier labs, where a single release can reset the field overnight.
poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.recent: The contract sits at 80% after peaking at 94% on Aug 31 and bottoming at 78% on Aug 11 — a wide swing over the month. Nothing in the window explains the move on the merits of the models themselves; the surrounding news concerns prediction markets as an industry, from the Ninth Circuit ruling that Kalshi's sports bets aren't "swaps" to a White House aide fined over speech bets.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether JD Vance will win the 2028 US presidential election, priced as a percentage. It is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field, the primaries and the incumbent's standing change.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.recent: The contract drifted from 20% on Aug 21 to 25% on Aug 30, ending at 24%, with nothing in the input explaining the move. The month's prediction-market news concerned the venues rather than the race: a White House aide paid a fine over bets on Trump's speeches, and the Ninth Circuit ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts are not "swaps.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A prediction market on who takes the Israeli premiership next. The price is what traders will pay for a contract that pays out if this candidate gets the job, so it tracks coalition arithmetic and defections rather than opinion polling.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The contract has stayed in a narrow band for the past month, between a low of 4% on Aug 7 and a high of 6% the following day, and it sits at the top of that range now. Nothing in the available reporting explains the shift.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by a set date. Traders price the odds; the strait carries about a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, so the bet is really on how long the disruption lasts.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: The price halved as the fighting resumed rather than settled: US strikes on Larak Island and Iranian launchers, a tanker-for-tanker targeting policy after two Iranian tankers were hit by US drones, a supertanker stopped by mines in the strait, and Iranian missiles on US bases in Jordan. Tehran now says transit requires its permission.

poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel will shut its civilian airspace before a set date. Traders price it as a proxy for war risk: closures follow missile exchanges and grounded airlines, so the number tracks how close the region looks to open conflict.
poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.recent: The contract drifted down over the window, from 12% on Aug 19 to a low of 6% on Aug 29 and 10% now, with the violence staying inside Gaza and the West Bank rather than spreading to exchanges of fire that would ground flights: strikes on a hospital compound, an airstrike on a Jenin home that killed 3 Palestinians, and Netanyahu's 'we are not retreating' visit.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged through the whole year. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever the case for easing weakens or strengthens.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: The no-cut price has barely moved across the month, holding near its highs while the debate underneath it shifted from cuts to hikes: an oil shock has pushed Fed hike odds to two-in-three, and Warsh said the Fed will have "work to do" if inflation doesn't fade.

poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Édouard Philippe, the former French prime minister who now leads his own party, wins the presidency in 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each shift in the French field.
poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.recent: The contract drifted from 25% on Aug 24 to 30% on Sep 4, an 11.5% rise over the month, with no single event in the window to account for it. Polymarket itself was the news: a report on 21 August found 152 wallets trading war outcomes at a 97.2% win rate.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether US crypto market-structure legislation known as the Clarity Act is enacted during 2026. It prices how far Congress has actually got, and the rules it would set decide which regulator oversees digital-asset trading.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The odds slid after a bad fortnight for the prediction-market industry the bill would touch. On 28 August the Ninth Circuit ruled in San Francisco that sports bets are not "swaps", confirming state powers over prediction markets, and Connecticut added its own lawsuit against Kalshi the day before. On 29 August a White House aide was fined over betting on the president's speeches.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pete Buttigieg becomes the Democratic nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each shift in the field rather than with any poll.
poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.recent: The move is small — from 5% in early August to 6% on 2 September — and nothing in the field explains it. What has changed is the venue: on 28 August the Ninth Circuit ruled that sports bets are not "swaps", confirming state powers over prediction markets, and a Connecticut lawsuit against Kalshi followed.

wiki-turkey.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Turkey. It rises when the country is in the news, so the shape of the curve is a rough map of which Turkish stories reached a global audience.
wiki-turkey.recent: The peak on Aug 31 came as the first committee under the Mecca defence pact met in Istanbul, with Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia working out what the agreement means, and as a ferry carrying 260 passengers capsized off northern Cyprus. Readership eased after, then a cargo ship sank in a collision off Istanbul with 10 crew missing.

poly-will-the-fed-decrease-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve lowers its policy rate after October 2026. The price is what traders are paying for that outcome, and it moves with every signal about inflation and the cost of borrowing.
poly-will-the-fed-decrease-interest-rate.recent: Brent near $95–97 on the resumed Iran strikes inverted the question: markets moved from expecting a Fed cut to pricing a possible hike this month, and hike odds jumped to two-in-three. Warsh added that the Fed will have "work to do" if inflation doesn't fade — an oil shock is an inflation shock, and one policy rate cannot tell the two apart.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if crude oil sets a new record price by a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with anything that threatens supply — a war, a sanction, a closed strait.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: The contract has drifted down over the past month, from 14% on Aug 19 to 10%, with no supply event in the window to lift it. What news there was concerned the venues rather than the barrel: a White House aide was fined over bets placed on the president's speeches, and judges in San Francisco ruled sports bets aren't "swaps".

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built for privacy: unlike bitcoin, its ledger hides sender, receiver and amount, so transactions cannot be traced by inspecting the chain. That property makes it the settlement layer of choice for ransomware and sanctions evasion.
xmr.recent: The rise tracks demand from actors who need untraceable payment. A group calling itself VantaCore has hit at least seven Russian companies with custom ransomware, and North Korea now earns without touching banks, moving revenue through channels no correspondent bank can freeze. The peak of $520.6 came on Sep 1.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares in the American electric-car maker, which also sells energy storage and is valued heavily on its self-driving ambitions rather than the cars it delivers today. Regulators, recalls and robotaxi milestones move it more than quarterly volumes.
stocks:TSLA.recent: The stock ran to $376.40 on Sep 3, the day Tesla began carrying paying passengers in the Cybercab in Austin — a production car with no steering wheel and no pedals, put into commercial service before the exemption process for such vehicles concluded. The August low came as China ordered a recall of 3 million Teslas over flush door handles.
